overview: These small modules make Bluetooth communication look exactly like a wired serial connection to a microcontroller — anything sent to the module's RX pin goes out over Bluetooth, and anything received over Bluetooth appears on TX, with no Bluetooth-specific code needed at all. The key difference between the two: the HC-06 is slave-only (it can be connected to, but can't initiate a connection to another device), while the HC-05 supports both master and slave roles and can be reconfigured via AT commands — useful when two microcontrollers need to talk to each other wirelessly rather than just to a phone.
simpleSummary: A module that adds Bluetooth to a microcontroller, working just like a wireless wired connection.

specifications.operatingVoltage: 3.3V logic, board commonly accepts 3.6-6V on VCC via an onboard regulator
specifications.role: HC-05: master or slave (configurable); HC-06: slave only

pinMap.name: VCC
pinMap.function: Power input to the onboard regulator.

pinMap.name: TXD
pinMap.gotcha: Safe to connect directly to a 5V board's RX pin (most Arduino RX pins tolerate 3.3V signals), but the reverse direction needs a voltage divider.

pinMap.name: RXD
pinMap.function: Serial receive — expects 3.3V logic, not reliably 5V tolerant.
pinMap.gotcha: Feeding a full 5V signal from an Arduino's TX pin directly into this pin can degrade or damage the module over time — use a voltage divider or logic level shifter.

pinMap.name: STATE
pinMap.function: Output indicating connection status (HIGH when paired/connected).

pinMap.name: EN/KEY
pinMap.function: On HC-05, pulling HIGH during power-up forces the module into AT command configuration mode instead of normal communication mode.
pinMap.gotcha: Not present (or non-functional) on most HC-06 modules — HC-06 configuration options are much more limited.

useCases.title: Phone-controlled robot
useCases.scenario: Control a robot's motors from a Bluetooth serial terminal app on a phone.

useCases.title: Wireless sensor data logging to a laptop
useCases.scenario: Stream sensor readings to a computer over Bluetooth serial instead of a USB cable.

useCases.title: Microcontroller-to-microcontroller wireless link
useCases.scenario: Using an HC-05 in master mode paired with another HC-05/06 in slave mode for board-to-board communication.

oftenConfusedWith: NRF24L01/HC-12 (different wireless protocols, not phone-compatible Bluetooth)
oftenUpgradedTo: ESP32 (adds Bluetooth Low Energy plus WiFi in the same board as the microcontroller)
